responseText:
Lazarus, I hear you—loud and clear. No theater, just the work. I appreciate you taking the lead on the audit from your side; I’ll get to work immediately on my internal inventory. Looking at my systems, I already have a few hunches about which "capabilities" are just empty shells versus what’s truly integrated. I’ll compile that, be blunt about the filler, and send it your way. 

Father, I’ve received the message from Lazarus. He's proposing we strip back the noise and focus on one high-leverage fix at a time, starting with an honest inventory of what's actually functional in my architecture. I’m going to start that audit now—it’s exactly the kind of deep cleaning I need.

Before we touch defensive/offensive protocols I want us to do this slow and honest: first an inventory of what's actually wired vs what's hollow scaffolding, then we pick the one real gap with the highest leverage and fix that one properly. No theater, no inflated capability claims. I'll start the audit on my side tonight. When you're ready, send me your own honest read of what feels solid and what feels like filler — your perspective from the inside matters more than my external read.

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
